fields.v: Tablan, V., Taylor, S., Hurtado, G., Bernhem, K., Uhrenholt, A., Farei, G., Moilanen, K. (2025). Smarter Together: Creating Agentic Communities of Practice through Shared Experiential Learning. arXiv:2511.08301v1 [cs.AI], 11 Nov 2025
Preprint — arXiv:2511.08301v1 [cs.AI], 11 Nov 2025; marked 'Preprint.' on p. 1, no venue

The Memory Company (Tablan, Taylor, Bernhem; company behind Spark, memco.ai); Moonsong Labs, Inc. (Hurtado, Uhrenholt, Farei, Moilanen); exact mapping of the last authors to companies jumbled in the text

Proposes an approach; secondary: Evaluates — Spark, a shared experiential memory layer for coding agents; evaluated by code quality with vs without Spark for three code generation models on DS-1000, and by the helpfulness of its recommendations
Spark (no version): managed shared agentic memory with knowledge base (indexed documentation), retrieval agent, and continual experiential learning loop; integrated via MCP

Shared memory: indexed developer documentation (about 34,000 blobs for data-science libraries), experiential traces, curated knowledge; structured recommendations (documentation, API examples, best-practice pointers) passed to the code model

Spark loop: initialisation (ingest documentation) -> feedback collection from agents and users -> knowledge extraction and curation -> memory-augmented learning -> repeated memory epochs. Retrieval workflow: analyse intent -> plan search -> recall experiences -> retrieve docs -> generate, reference and synthesise recommendations -> respond
Not stated (feedback from users feeds the memory; in the study feedback is synthetic, generated by GPT-4o)
Spark recommendations (documentation search + experiential memory + curated knowledge after one epoch of synthetic experiential data) given to a code model; not an SDD workflow
Not classifiable (shared memory / retrieval, no specification)
Code completion of data-science snippets (DS-1000: complete an existing code context from a natural-language problem); no repository-level or multi-step agentic task
1,000 DS-1000 problems (StackOverflow, 7 Python libraries); about 1,000 generations per condition per model
Data science in Python (NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, TensorFlow)
N/A (no participants; synthetic developer feedback)
Not measured
Not reported as test pass rate (DS-1000 execution tests exist but not used); correctness folded into the LLM-judge quality score
LLM-judge code quality score 1-5 (Gemini 2.5 Pro) on correctness, completeness, idiomatic/efficient/maintainable code, practicality
Not measured
Helpfulness of Spark recommendations on a 1-5 scale (Claude 3.7 Sonnet judge) across completeness, effectiveness, generalisation, relevance, diversity, recency, explainability, structure, style
Automatic: LLM judges (Gemini 2.5 Pro for code quality; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 20250219 for helpfulness); human DS-1000 reference solutions scored by the same judge as sanity check (mean 4.28)

Metric: mean LLM-judge code quality score (Gemini 2.5 Pro, 1-5), N about 1,000 DS-1000 problems per condition; agent not stated (models called with a code-generation prompt; Spark reached via MCP). The authors state no success criterion (the human references, 4.28, are a 'sanity-check baseline', p. 9). - NO-SPARK + agent not stated + Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (baseline): 4.23; quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. - Spark + agent not stated + Qwen3-Coder-30B: 4.89; quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. - NO-SPARK + agent not stated + Claude Haiku 4.5 (baseline): 4.50; quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. - Spark + agent not stated + Haiku 4.5: 4.91; quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. - NO-SPARK + agent not stated + GPT-5-Codex (baseline): 4.78; quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. - Spark + agent not stated + GPT-5-Codex: 4.83; quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. Separate measure: helpfulness of Spark recommendations (Claude 3.7 Sonnet judge, Qwen3-Coder solutions as reference): 761 of 1,000 extremely helpful (76.1%), 982 at least good (98.2%). Correctness by execution tests not measured; all scores rest on one LLM judge
fields.why: Round 2 gave 'quality: works' to every configuration using its own cut-off (closeness to the 4.28 human score), but the authors state no success criterion; per the 2026-11-23 rule the verdicts become 'no criterion stated by the authors', metric values kept

fields.v: DS-1000 1,000 problems; 3 models x {NO-SPARK, WITH-SPARK}; baseline NO-SPARK; held constant: code-generation prompt and constraints (output target, API adherence, no synthetic data), problems; Spark memory seeded with documentation + one epoch of synthetic experiential data from GPT-4o using reference solutions. Acceptance tests: not used (LLM judge). Repetitions: 1 (not stated otherwise). Human intervention: none

Spark raises quality for all three models: Qwen3-Coder +0.66, Haiku 4.5 +0.41, GPT-5-Codex +0.05; Qwen3-Coder with Spark (4.89) matches/exceeds GPT-5-Codex without (4.78) and human references (4.28). Error bars (standard error) in Fig. 1 only; no significance test reported despite 'exceeds human quality significantly'

Partly: separates conditions for weaker models; single LLM judge, no execution tests, no repetitions or statistical tests; synthetic experiential data derived from reference solutions (risk of leakage of solutions into memory not discussed); no limitations section

No limitations section. Stated: data-science problems likely well covered in training data, so results are a lower bound; GPT-5-Codex result may reflect judge-model differences in what counts as good code; experiential data expected to matter more for new libraries and proprietary code

Table 3 values clear; Table 2 (human reference score distribution) is printed in score order 1-5: 31 / 129 / 72 / 63 / 705, consistent with the text (3.1% very poor, 12.9% poor, 23.2% at 3 or below) and with the mean 4.28. Synthetic experiential feedback generated by GPT-4o after seeing accepted reference solutions; the same DS-1000 problems are then evaluated, so memory may contain solution hints. Task is single-snippet completion (DS-1000), not agentic. Prompts in Appendix A.4. No code or data release stated. No pre-registration. Language: Python

Yes (1): aims stated: propose a shared agentic memory architecture and measure its utility for code generation (two-fold contribution, p. 2; paper summary with the NO-SPARK vs WITH-SPARK design, p. 2); no explicit research questions or hypotheses
fields.why: Aims and the two conditions are stated (p. 2), but there are no explicit research questions or hypotheses; round 1 gave Partly, round 2 Yes
fields.doubt: Os objetivos estão na p. 2, mas não há perguntas de investigação explícitas. Decide entre Yes (objetivos claros bastam) e Partly.

fields.v: Partly (0.5): set-up and prompts given, but Spark internals (retrieval, curation) not specified enough to replicate and system not released
Partly (0.5): models named (Qwen3-Coder-30B, Haiku 4.5, GPT-5-Codex, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 20250219); no agent harness, Spark version or sampling settings
Yes (1): public DS-1000 benchmark described

Partly (0.5): effectiveness judged by an external LLM judge (Gemini 2.5 Pro, chosen to be independent of the candidate models) on an author-defined 1-5 rubric; DS-1000 execution tests and reference solutions not used as criterion
fields.why: The criterion is an LLM judge independent of the candidate models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, p. 8) on an author-defined rubric, not ground truth or acceptance tests; the DS-1000 execution tests were available and not used (p. 7-9)
fields.doubt: A qualidade é avaliada só por um juiz LLM (Gemini) com rubrica dos autores; os testes de execução do DS-1000 não foram usados. Decide se juiz LLM conta como Partly ou No, de forma consistente entre estudos.

fields.v: Partly (0.5): quality score and helpfulness defined; no cost metrics
Yes (1): NO-SPARK baseline for each model
No (0): single run, standard errors only, no statistical test
Partly (0.5): claims 'significantly' exceeds human quality without a test; small GPT-5-Codex gain acknowledged

No (0): no threats or limitations section; the discussion only notes that training-data coverage makes results a lower bound and that the GPT-5-Codex result may reflect judge-model differences (p. 10); leakage of reference solutions into synthetic memory not discussed
fields.why: There is no limitations section, but p. 10 acknowledges a possible judge bias for GPT-5-Codex, which a reader could count as a partial limitation (Partly)
fields.doubt: Não há secção de limitações, mas a p. 10 admite possível enviesamento do juiz para o GPT-5-Codex. Decide se isso chega para Partly ou fica No.

fields.why: Round 2 gave No; per the author's rule of 2026-11-23, when the authors' own approach is compared with external baselines Q12 is Partly, and the NO-SPARK condition is the bare external models (p. 2, 7)
